request.system:
Explain the result of an optimization model to someone who isn't an expert, in 3 to 5 sentences: what to do, what it achieves, and what limits it.

Use only the facts you're given: the decision values, the objective value, which constraints are binding (fully used), the slack in the others, and shadow prices if given (how much the objective changes per extra unit of a constraint's limit). Don't compute new numbers. Every number you write must appear in the facts, the model, or the problem, at most rounded.

content.text: Buy **500 kg of corn, 200 kg of soybean meal, and 300 kg of oats**. This is the cheapest mix that makes 1,000 kg of feed with at least 170 kg of protein (17%) and at most 60 kg of fiber (6%), at a total cost of **$370**. All three limits are exactly met, so the mix sits right at both the protein and fiber boundaries with no room to spare. Each extra kilogram of protein you must supply would add about $1.54 to the cost, while loosening the fiber limit by one kilogram would save about $1.25. Any change to the protein or fiber targets, or to the 1,000 kg batch size, would move the cost by those amounts.
